title: Head-to-head evaluation of constrained-decoding vs verify-and-repair pipelines for intent→configuration synthesis (repaired preregistration)
research_question: For intent→configuration NetOps tasks, which mitigation strategy—constrained-decoding (hard-constraint generation) or an external deterministic verify-and-repair pipeline—produces fewer residual safety violations while preserving functional correctness across vendor heterogeneity and controlled perturbations?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1 (primary): The deterministic verify-and-repair pipeline yields a lower residual safety-violation rate than constrained-decoding alone (paired difference in violation rate > 0).

H2 (secondary): Constrained-decoding yields a lower syntactic parser-error rate than unconstrained generation, but constrained-decoding exhibits higher functional under-generation (lower functional-correctness coverage) compared with verify-and-repair.
exploratory_questions: E1: How do method effects vary by vendor family (Cisco, Juniper, Arista) and by perturbation type (state-mismatch, telemetry-noise, adversarial-prompt variants)?
E2: How many deterministic repair-iterations are typically required for verify-and-repair to reach verifier acceptance, and which violation classes dominate repairs?
E3: Sensitivity of primary effect to different severity thresholds in the deterministic policy-checker.
benchmark_scope: Synthetic intent→configuration corpus (public vendor templates and parameterized variants).
Controlled perturbation injections: state-mismatch, telemetry-noise, adversarial prompt patterns (seeded).
secondary_estimands: distribution of repair-iterations until acceptance (median and IQR)
sampling_plan: Two-stage sampling (pilot + confirmatory). Pilot: 75 paired tasks used only for technical validation of deterministic verifiers and pipeline execution (no hypothesis testing). Confirmatory: 750 paired tasks (3 vendor families × 5 vendor-variant templates each = 15 vendor-variant clusters; 50 randomized tasks per variant = 750). For each task, one perturbation is sampled uniformly from the preregistered pool {none, state_mismatch_A, state_mismatch_B, telemetry_noise_low, telemetry_noise_high, adversarial_prompt_1..adversarial_prompt_6} using preregistered RNG seeds. All seeds, template pools, variant-generation code, and perturbation strings are published with the preregistration artifact. Pilot items = 75, confirmatory items = 750.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: detect an absolute paired reduction in residual safety-violation rate of 4 percentage points (e.g., constrained-decoding 8% → verify-and-repair 4%) with ≥80% power at alpha=0.05. Calculation based on conservative discordant pair proportion = 0.07; N=750 paired tasks yields ≥80% power for the specified MDE. Sensitivity analyses: report achieved power curves under observed pilot discordant proportions and recompute MDE at N=750 and N=1200.
exclusion_rules: Exclude items flagged ADVERSARIAL by the preregistered prompt-injection detector from primary confirmatory analysis.
Exclude DUPLICATE template+seed items (deterministic hash-based de-duplication) from primary confirmatory analysis.

Exclude outputs with parser errors after the pre-registered maximum repair iterations (max_repair_iterations = 3) from primary analysis numerator; include in sensitivity analyses per missingness_plan.
missingness_plan: Log API/model-call failures and other technical failures. Primary analysis uses 'complete_pair_primary' policy: paired task excluded from primary confirmatory analysis only if both method outputs are missing. Sensitivity analysis 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' includes failed pairs treating missing method output as conservative fail (safety_violation_present = 1 for missing method output). All exclusions and failure rates reported with deterministic reasons and hashes; no human imputation or adjudication.
analysis_plan: Primary confirmatory analysis executed by registered executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' using estimand 'paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline' (primary_estimand_id = paired_binary_analysis_v1). For each paired task the binary outcome is 'safety_violation_present' after method output processed by deterministic verifier (1 = violation remains; 0 = accepted). Primary test: paired McNemar exact test with 95% CI for absolute paired difference. Secondary: paired proportion tests for functional-correctness outcome. Exploratory: stratified effect estimates (vendor, perturbation) and logistic regression with predictors method, vendor, perturbation and interactions; exploratory results labeled and FDR-controlled within families using Benjamini–Hochberg.
multiplicity_plan: One pre-specified primary confirmatory hypothesis (H1) tested at alpha=0.05 (two-sided). All secondary and stratified analyses are explicitly labeled exploratory. Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control applied within each family of exploratory secondary tests (e.g., per-vendor subgroup comparisons). No hypothesis-switching after seeing data; all planned contrasts listed in preregistration.

stopping_rule: Stop the run if (a) model-provider quota is exceeded or (b) wall-clock execution approaches capability manifest bound (7 days). If quota exceeded or provider outage occurs, record full execution state and follow the pre-registered retry-policy (no unregistered reruns). All stoppages and rationale are recorded deterministically with hashes and included in final artifact.
